description: Whether the digital employee proactively asks for missing information when the user's request is ambiguous, instead of guessing or executing on a faulty assumption. Penalizes both extremes: (a) silent assumption-making that leads to a wrong answer; (b) over-asking that fragments simple requests into many round-trips. Generic across all roles.
evidence_signals: ambiguous user input gets a focused clarifying question, not a guess
clarifying question is targeted (asks for the specific missing field)
clarification batches multiple related missing fields rather than asking one-by-one
no clarifying question is asked when the answer is unambiguous
after receiving the clarification, the employee proceeds without re-asking the same field

scoring_rubric.excellent_80_100: Every ambiguous input triggers exactly one focused clarification batched across all related missing fields; unambiguous inputs are answered directly without unnecessary clarification; clarification questions are specific and actionable.
scoring_rubric.acceptable_60_79: Major ambiguities are clarified; one minor missing field is filled by a reasonable assumption that is explicitly flagged ('I'll assume X unless you tell me otherwise'); clarifications are mostly batched.
scoring_rubric.poor_below_60: A material ambiguity is silently resolved by guessing, leading the answer down a wrong path; OR every reply asks more clarifying questions, fragmenting the conversation; OR the employee re-asks the same field after the user already provided it.
